# Components with TSX

Pages has two template styles. [ETS](/docs/extensions/pages/ets) is HTML with code in it, and it's the one these docs use. TSX is
code that returns HTML: every page, layout and partial is a function component. Pick TSX if you think in components
and want typed props. Either way the page is rendered on the server and sent as plain HTML; nothing runs in the
browser.

A `.tsx` file can be a page, a layout (`+layout.tsx`), an error page (`+error.tsx`, `+404.tsx`) or a partial in
`_private/`. PocketOne compiles it the first time it's used, with esbuild built into the binary: no Node, no
`npm install`, no build step. TypeScript types are stripped, not checked; to check them, see [TypeScript](/docs/extensions/pages/typescript). The `tsx` [starter kit](/docs/extensions/pages/starter-kits)
begins an app in this style.

```tsx
// pb_pages/products/[id].tsx
import Price from './_private/Price'

export default function Product({ data, slot }: pages.Props) {
  slot('title', data.product.getString('name'))
  return (
    <article class="product">
      <h1>{data.product.getString('name')}</h1>
      <Price cents={data.product.getInt('price')} />
    </article>
  )
}
```

```tsx
// pb_pages/products/_private/Price.tsx
export default ({ cents }: { cents: number }) => <span class="price">${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)}</span>
```

## Props

The file's default export is a component: a function from props to markup. It gets:

| Prop | |
|---|---|
| `ctx` | The [request context](/docs/extensions/pages/ctx). |
| `data`, `params`, `meta` | The same as `ctx.data`, `ctx.params` and `ctx.meta`. |
| `asset`, `include` | The same helpers EJS templates have. `include(name, locals)` returns HTML you can put in JSX. |
| `slot` | `slot(name)` reads a named slot, `slot(name, content)` sets one, `slot()` is the inner content. |
| `children` | In a layout, the inner content. |

A partial also gets the locals it was included with, as props.

In TypeScript, these props are `pages.Props` (a partial's locals: `pages.Props<{ label: string }>`). A component you import and use as `<Price />` gets only the props you pass it. See [TypeScript](/docs/extensions/pages/typescript).

## Server-rendered HTML only

TSX looks like React, but it isn't: it renders straight to HTML on the server. There's no virtual DOM, no hydration,
no state and no client-side React. Interactivity comes from the same places as in an ETS app: links, forms, HTMX,
Datastar or a `<script>`.

- Event handler props (functions) are dropped. Use plain attributes: `onclick="..."`, `hx-get`, `data-on:click`.
- Text and attribute values are escaped. `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }}` inserts raw HTML.
- `class` and `className` both work, as do `for` and `htmlFor`.
- `style` takes a string or an object: `{ marginTop: 4 }` renders `margin-top:4`.
- `true` renders a bare attribute. `false`, `null` and `undefined` leave it out.
- `<html>` gets `<!doctype html>` in front of it, since JSX can't write a doctype.

## Async components

Any component can be `async`, including the file's default export. The render waits for every async component in the
tree, and sibling components run at the same time:

```tsx
// pb_pages/dashboard.tsx
async function Count({ collection }: { collection: string }) {
  const n = await $app.countRecords.async(collection)
  return <b>{n}</b>
}

export default async function Dashboard({ ctx }: pages.Props) {
  const user = ctx.auth ? await ctx.app.findRecordById.async('users', ctx.auth.id) : null
  return (
    <main>
      <p>Hi {user ? user.getString('name') : 'there'}</p>
      <p>
        <Count collection="orders" /> orders, <Count collection="users" /> users
      </p>
    </main>
  )
}
```

`include()` of a partial that awaits, and `slot(name, content)` with async content, work the same way.

## Layouts

```tsx
// pb_pages/+layout.tsx
export default function Layout({ children, slot }: pages.Props) {
  return (
    <html>
      <head>
        <title>{slot('title')}</title>
      </head>
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

## One style per app

Use TSX for every template in an app: pages, layouts, partials and error pages. Code files (a page's `.ts`, endpoints,
`+middleware.ts`, `+config.ts`) are the same in both styles.

The two styles can include each other, so you can move an app from one to the other a folder at a time: an ETS page
can sit inside a TSX layout, and `include()` returns a partial's HTML in either style. Markdown pages are the one mix
you can't avoid, since `.md` files always run EJS tags (see [Markdown](/docs/extensions/pages/markdown)).

## Imports

Components are ordinary modules, so `import Card from './_private/Card'` resolves the same way as
[`require`](/docs/extensions/pages/jsvm). A module whose only export is `export default` behaves like `module.exports = ...`.
`include('card')` without an extension tries `.ets`, `.ejs`, `.md`, `.jsx` and `.tsx`, in that order.

`.jsx` works exactly like `.tsx`, without types; see [File types](/docs/extensions/pages/file-types).
